name: Glossary
title: Glossary
subtitle: What does every term and metric on this report mean?

paras.t: The unit of Copilot consumption metered by Microsoft. Both products bill in credits, but they are metered and reported separately.
Billing a group only for the credits its people used above their limit. Usage within the limit is not charged.
The cost of one credit, set in Settings (default $0.01). Cowork and Studio each have their own pay-as-you-go and prepaid rates.

Two separate caps. User limits add up each person's own monthly credit limit. Policy limits add up the plan limits on the spending policies. They are different numbers and the report labels which one it is showing.
Credits bought up front. Microsoft calls this entitlement in the Studio admin centre and a capacity pack for Copilot. Usage draws this down first; anything beyond it bills pay-as-you-go.
Credits, and their cost, used above the limit. This is the chargeable amount.
Credits inside a limit that were never used — candidates to reduce or move elsewhere.
Credits above the limit as a share of the limit — how far a group went over.
A group's share of all credits used across the org.
A user's credits divided by their department's average. 9.8 means 9.8 times the department norm.
Users with activity in the last 30 days.

Prepaid credits are drawn from capacity already bought. Pay-as-you-go is everything beyond that, billed in arrears. The Studio pages report the split because Microsoft reports it; on Cowork it is inferred from the capacity pack balance you enter.
How long the prepaid capacity lasts at the current daily rate, counting only environments that hold capacity. Environments with none bill directly and cannot run it down.
A suggestion per agent, from how much it consumes and how much of that is chargeable: Review, Investigate, Monitor, Healthy, or Unused.
The share of an agent's credits absorbed by prepaid capacity, so they never reached a bill.
Filters the user figures only. The agent and environment exports carry no person, so those figures stay unfiltered.
What acting on a recommendation is worth each month: the credits released by reclaiming and downsizing, less the cost of the upgrades. Buckets marked no action are zero by definition.
Capacity that could be released if every oversized seat were resized. A measure of slack, not an action -- it counts headroom wherever it sits.
Capacity assigned to seats with no usage in the billing snapshot. One period only, so treat it as a list to check rather than a list to cancel.
Consumption normalised to a month. The four products are exported over different windows, so the All products page compares run rates rather than raw totals.

Costs are also expressed as FinOps FOCUS v1.2 columns on the FOCUS Cost View page: List Cost (list rate), Contracted Cost = Chargeback $ (configured rate), Effective / Billed Cost, and Savings vs List; Service = Microsoft 365 Copilot, Service Category = AI and Machine Learning, Billing Currency = USD, SubAccount = Department / Cost Center.

A group is charged only for the credits its people used above their limit. Usage within the limit is not billed, so an org-wide figure under 100% does not mean nothing is chargeable — individuals can still exceed their own limit.
= List Cost minus Contracted Cost; it is $0 while the configured rate equals the $0.01 list rate.
